Cornyn and Tillis had previously blocked the nomination, demanding written confirmation that the fund—created in May to compensate Trump's political allies—would be permanently terminated amid bipartisan criticism over potential payments to January 6 rioters.

Blanche's Sunday order confirms "No Members were appointed; no funds were transferred; no process for receiving claims was established; no claims were paid." The order clarifies tax audit immunity "applies by its terms only retroactively" and does not shield future filings.

Democratic Sen. Adam Schiff and other critics argue the deal lacks enforcement, warning the fund could be revived and that Trump retains an "unprecedented, unconscionable benefit" from the tax immunity provision despite the formal rescission.

Explosive winds and dry terrain fueled the Autumn Lane, Fairview, and Old Trails fires, which erupted Saturday and rapidly jumped the Spokane River, spreading flames through suburban neighborhoods.
About 10,000 residents remained without electricity Sunday as Avista Corp worked to repair damaged transmission lines, while about 400 people sought shelter at the Spokane Convention Center.

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson declared a state of emergency and coordinated with President Donald Trump for federal resources, while U.S. Sen. Maria Cantwell designated the disaster the nation's top wildfire priority.
Hot, dry weather is expected to persist through the coming week, complicating efforts for the more than 900 personnel currently battling uncontained blazes across Eastern Washington.
title: Fast moving wildfires raze neighborhoods in US northwest city of Spokane

summary: On Aug 3, the Michigan Department reported two deaths linked to cyclosporiasis, stating both individuals had underlying health conditions that "may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration."

Cyclosporiasis is a seasonal diarrheal illness caused by a parasite that commonly causes "explosive diarrhea" and hides in the rough, irregular surfaces of fresh produce like leafy greens and berries.
The CDC reports an acceleration of United States food-related illnesses this year, though no single source has been identified as the parasite is increasingly found on domestically grown produce.
Dr. Steven Goldberg of HealthTrackRx recommends manually cleaning produce under forceful water, avoiding bleach; he notes "prewashed" produce does not require additional washing at home.
With the cyclosporiasis season lasting through Aug 31, consumers should refrigerate cut or cooked produce within two hours to minimize illness risks during the remainder of the active season.
title: Michigan reports two deaths in ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak

Investigators linked Farinacci to the blaze after a witness reported seeing him kneeling in grass near Euclid Road and Old Trails Road just before the fire erupted around 10 a.m. Saturday.

When initially detained Saturday, Farinacci possessed waterproof matches and a butane lighter, Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels said; records show the suspect has a prior felony manslaughter conviction from Arizona.
Held on $1 million bail, Farinacci is scheduled to make his first court appearance today, Tuesday, at Spokane County court.
The Old Trails Fire remains 0% contained, part of a regional crisis that has destroyed over 700 structures and forced nearly 67,000 evacuations across Spokane County as firefighting efforts continue.

Authorities received a 911 call around 2:30 p.m. reporting a man climbing the structure, prompting police to discover a Kazakh flag and a blanket marked with incoherent writing left at the tower.
Emergency responders transported Abaildayev to Bellevue Hospital for treatment, where medical staff reported him in stable condition following the rescue from the East River.

Police charged Abaildayev with reckless endangerment, public lewdness, criminal trespass, and disorderly conduct, while authorities immediately closed pedestrian traffic on the Brooklyn Bridge during the incident.
The incident occurred less than a month after a separate rescue on the same Brooklyn Bridge involving a distressed person, with police currently investigating the circumstances.

The CIA and other U.S. agencies have assessed with low confidence that COVID-19 most likely originated from a laboratory, though this finding is disputed among experts and not based on new intelligence.

title: Ex-Biden Adviser Says Pandemic Was Likely a Lab Leak

Defense attorney Carrie Slinkard expressed disappointment, stating the grand jury proceeding was 'conducted in secret' with no defense opportunity to present evidence. Ben Crump, representing the family, has called the shooting 'unjustifiable.'
The Aurora Police Department remains under a court-ordered consent decree following past misconduct, while Belt-Stubblefield's family is suing the City of Aurora for at least $20 million in damages.
title: Aurora officer indicted on murder charge in 2025 fatal shooting

Under the terms of reference, the review will evaluate public communications, customer service standards, and the agency's ability to meet changing needs of the Australian community.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio has portrayed these measures as necessary to right-size an organization many conservatives see as bloated; some officials privately argue smaller missions are inessential and not cost effective.

The closures involve an embassy in Grenada, plus consulates and a branch office elsewhere, while China maintains a diplomatic presence in St. George's, Nagoya, and Medan but lacks missions in Douala or Winnipeg.

Democrats and former foreign policy officials argue the cuts, coupled with dismantling the Agency for International Development, risk undermining American leadership and leave a dangerous vacuum for adversaries like Russia and China.

Early last year, the Donald Trump administration began preparing to close nearly a dozen missions aligned with an "America First" agenda, while the White House Office of Management and Budget had advocated targeting up to 30 foreign missions.

Senate appropriators remain deadlocked over topline spending figures and have yet to pass any of the 12 annual funding bills, making the continuing resolution necessary to provide time for fiscal year 2027 negotiations.

Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins secured a provision blocking a Trump administration proposal to grant political appointees final authority over scientific grants, earning bipartisan backing.

The House previously passed a shorter continuing resolution last month without these provisions, requiring the chamber to take up the Senate bill when it returns in September to reconcile the differences.
This stopgap measure keeps government funding at current levels through Dec. 11, providing leadership additional time to negotiate before departing for a month-long recess at week's end.
title: Senate overwhelmingly advances stopgap funding bill aimed at preventing shutdown

Federal scrutiny of higher education persists through ongoing investigations into medical schools for 'alleged racial discrimination,' alongside broader efforts to combat grade inflation and address 'politicized' scholarship in humanities departments.

During her tenure, Paxson oversaw endowment growth to $8 billion and directed more than $2 billion in campus investments, including approximately $700 million in Jewelry District redevelopment.
Her leadership navigated a December 2025 campus shooting that killed two students and a federal funding freeze, after which Paxson resolved a $510 million grant dispute in July 2025.
Brown University Chancellor Brian Moynihan announced the Brown Corporation will launch a national search for Paxson's successor, aligning with a new strategic planning cycle.

title: Aaron Rodgers: Fauci a ‘coward’ and a ‘criminal’ for taking the Fifth

summary: On Monday, August 3, 2026, President Donald Trump declared new talks with Iran represent a 'last chance' to avoid further military escalation, threatening 'decapitation' if Tehran fails to sign a deal.

Trump recently suspended a massive military strike he described as 'the biggest attack since World War II' after Gulf allies Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Qatar urged him to pursue diplomacy.

Negotiations target reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing Iran's nuclear program, though Tehran's Foreign Ministry publicly denied U.S. discussions, claiming it only communicates with Oman regarding safe maritime routes.
Senator Mark Kelly called Trump's approach 'rather erratic,' while Senator John Kennedy warned that further escalation could trigger 'a lot of inflation for the American people.'

Trump maintains military action remains an option 'anytime we want,' while Iran attempts to outlast U.S. pressure ahead of November's midterm elections amid concerns over diminished munitions stockpiles.
title: Trump says Iran facing ‘last chance’ before ‘decapitation’

summary: On Tuesday, Jonathan Veitch, head of UNICEF for the Palestinian territories, reported that Israeli water infrastructure restrictions are squandering Canadian aid, citing destruction of the Canada Well facility.

Israel restricts items like cement and generators as 'dual-use' materials to prevent Hamas from building weapons, forcing UNICEF to become the 'provider of last resort' for water and sanitation services across Gaza.

Veitch described dire conditions where families live in makeshift tents surrounded by waste, with nighttime temperatures seldom dropping below 25 C and "millions and millions of rats" infesting the area.
The Israeli Defense Forces stated last week it is assessing infrastructure damage with severity, while 2.1 million Gazans remain confined to 30 per cent of the territory facing critical shortages.

Canada "punches above its weight" in humanitarian assistance, Veitch said, noting private donations helped end a recent famine, though he warned peace remains elusive as thousands grow up without education.
title: UNICEF Official Says Gaza Water Restrictions Waste Canadian Aid

summary: The United States sent a repatriation flight to Venezuela, the first such flight since deadly earthquakes ravaged the South American nation in late June.

The Trump administration had been deporting hundreds of Venezuelans per week prior to June, but the deportation drive halted after back-to-back over 7-magnitude earthquakes killed more than 6,000 people.
Departing from Miami, the 165th flight carried 147 migrants to General Jos Antonio Anzo International Airport in Barcelona, Anzo.

Mervin Maldonado, head of the repatriation program, welcomed the migrants in a social media post, saying they are "returning home, to reunite with their families, to continue their education, to be productive, and to contribute to national development."
Venezuela faces a multi-year recovery following the twin quakes, which caused an economic hit equivalent to 6% of the country's GDP according to the United Nations Development Programme.
title: US Deports Venezuelans for the First Time Since Deadly Earthquakes in June

summary: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. launched The Real Food Show, a digital cooking series supporting the White House-backed "Make America Healthy Again" agenda.

Kennedy designed the program to demonstrate his dietary guidelines, which prioritize animal proteins and traditional fats while discouraging industrial seed oils, aiming for recipes costing under $5 per serving.
Detractors argue the celebrity-style production ignores systemic challenges like food deserts and rising grocery costs, while critics note Kennedy lacks a medical or professional dietary background.

This initiative aligns with President Donald Trump's pattern of appointing celebrities to government roles, including Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, Mehmet Oz, Linda McMahon, and Defense Pete Hegseth.
Rising measles cases and a cyclospora outbreak, which the Centers for Disease Control stopped monitoring last year under Kennedy's watch, persist alongside the administration's media initiatives.
title: RFK Jr. Talks Nutrition, Meat Consumption, and Vegan Diets

summary: On Monday, Aug. 3, Maria Cornejo announced that her son, Edwin Lopez Cornejo, died Aug. 1 at Delaney Hall detention center in Newark after being detained since June 18.

The 1,000-bed Delaney Hall facility has faced national scrutiny over reports of alleged medical neglect and abuse; this death marks the second recorded fatality since last December when Haitian national Jean Wilson Brutus died.
Maria Cornejo attributed her son's death to lack of diabetes medication while detained; he had lived in the United States for nearly 20 years and was the father of a 12-year-old girl.
Rep. LaMonica McIver denounced the death as a "pattern of abuse and neglect," stating "cruelty is at its core," and vowed to continue working to shut down Delaney Hall and abolish ICE.

This facility serves as a flashpoint in President Trump's immigration enforcement escalation, which has equipped ICE with a budget surpassing the militaries of all but 15 countries; the Department of Homeland Security has not responded to requests for comment.
title: Detainee dies at Delaney Hall ICE detention center: NJ senator

summary: On Monday, President Donald Trump publicly defended Rep. Max Miller amid domestic abuse accusations from his ex-wife, characterizing the situation as "a very sad thing."
Rep. Miller faces abuse claims from his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and pressure from her father, Sen. Bernie Moreno, though the congressman denies the allegations, saying he has "nothing to hide."

Amid mounting GOP concerns about Miller's electability, top House Republicans contacted White House officials for help, though Trump refused to publicly call for the congressman's resignation.
If Miller fails to withdraw by close of business Tuesday, party leaders face a narrow window to replace him before the August 10 deadline, threatening GOP control of the Ohio seat.
title: Trump praises Max Miller, calls dispute with ex-wife ‘a very sad thing’

summary: Morocco has officially renamed its 1,055km Tiznit-Dakhla expressway the "Donald J. Trump Highway." His Majesty King Mohammed confirmed the change, calling the road a "strategic axis" linking north and south Morocco.

The renaming honors President Donald Trump for his historic 2020 recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over the Moroccan Sahara. King Mohammed presented the gesture as a symbol of friendship between the Kingdom and the United States.

Costing nearly $1bn, the massive infrastructure project is described as "The largest road infrastructure in Africa." King Mohammed highlighted the gesture as "a personal expression of my high regard" for the president.
President Trump responded on Truth Social, thanking the monarch for "this great honor." He wrote, "I look forward to traveling the entire length of this great highway someday, hopefully soon!"

Western Sahara remains a former Spanish colony fought over for five decades. While the UN considers it a "non-self-governing territory," the Polisario Front continues seeking independence for the local Sahrawi people.
title: Morocco names major highway after Trump amid dispute over Western Sahara

summary: On Monday, five federal workers filed a class-action lawsuit against the Trump administration in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, challenging the Office of Personnel Management's ban on gender-affirming care coverage.

The Office of Personnel Management implemented this policy at the start of this year, prohibiting coverage for the "chemical and surgical modification of an individual's sex traits" and expanding restrictions to all federal employees and dependents.

State Department employee Gregory Goe faces more than $100,000 in costs for hormone therapy, while the Williams Institute estimates at least 39,400 transgender federal employees, retirees, and dependents could be affected by the exclusion.

HRCF President Kelley Robinson argued the ban violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which prohibits discrimination "because of" sex, contending federal health insurance is a term of employment.

The plaintiffs seek an injunction to reverse the policy and restore coverage, though the Supreme Court upheld restrictions on transgender procedures for minors last year, creating uncertain precedent for this broader challenge.
title: Trump administration sued for banning gender transition treatments in federal health plans

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Prop. 40 as a significant Democratic policy fight, stressing “deepening party divisions” and Newsom-labor pushback, while right-leaning coverage turns the same vote into a story of rebellion and overreach, with phrases like “defy,” “class warfare,” and “confiscation tax” casting the measure as ideological combat.

summary: On Sunday, the California Democratic Party executive board endorsed Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on billionaire assets designed to fund healthcare and restore safety-net programs.
The measure aims to raise an estimated $100 billion to replace healthcare funding slashed by President Donald Trump's budget bill last year, which eliminated coverage for over a million Californians.

Dave Regan, President of SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West, cited internal polling showing more than 80% of registered Democrats support the tax, while Public Policy Institute of California data indicates 54% of likely voters favor it.

Opposing the measure, Gov. Gavin Newsom and Xavier Becerra warn of potential budget instability, while wealthy opponents have funded competing initiatives, Propositions 41 and 42, to undermine the tax.

Democrats also voted to oppose a voter ID measure and a proposal to weaken the California Environmental Quality Act, while endorsing an $11.25-billion affordable housing bond and an $8.4-billion immunology research bond.
title: California Democratic Party backs billionaire tax despite internal opposition
